etymologies.etymologyHTML: Clipping of pianoforte, from Italian pianoforte, from piano (“soft”) + forte (“strong”). So named because it could produce a wide range of varied volumes note-by-note, in contrast to older keyboard instruments, notably the harpsichord. Doublet of llano, plain, and plane.

definitions.definition: (music) A percussive keyboard musical instrument, usually ranging over seven octaves, with white and black colored keys, played by pressing these keys, causing hammers to strike strings. [from  1803]

quote.citation: 1967, Harry F. Chaplin, A McCrae Miscellany, page 41:
quote.text: Anyhow I pianoed to my own ear, and had no thought at that time for an audience.

quote.citation: 1978, Bertha Harris, Confessions of Cherubino, page 96:
quote.text: Who comforted me with Madeleines and lime tea, with whipped cream in my cocoa in far off Ann Arbor while others selfishly fiddled, bassooned, pianoed only for their own ugly self-advancement!

definitions.definition: (of or with fingers) To move (the fingers) up and down on, similar to the motions of a pianist playing the piano.

definitions.definition: (music) Softly, as a dynamic in a piece of music. [from 17th c.]
